reference.label: Reference
reference.note: All features, trees stopped early, all history, ratio target.

trees_10.note: Ten trees: the model has barely begun to fit.

trees_50.note: Fifty trees. On the held-out days this scores better than the reference, which stops later on its validation block.

trees_200.note: Two hundred trees: still short of where the reference stops, and ahead of it on the held-out days.

trees_3000.note: No early stopping: training error keeps falling after validation error has stopped.

lags_only.label: Lags only
lags_only.note: Only the ride series against its own past. No clock, no weather.

lags_calendar.label: Plus calendar
lags_calendar.note: Lags and the calendar of the hour forecast. No weather.

months_1.label: 1 month
months_1.note: Trained on the last month before the stop block.

months_3.label: 3 months
months_3.note: Trained on the last three months.

months_6.label: 6 months
months_6.note: Trained on the last six months.

counts.label: Ride counts
counts.note: Asked for rides, not for the ratio to last week. Trees extrapolate poorly beyond the count levels in their training rows.

no_local.label: None
no_local.note: Trained on other cities and generated demand. It has never seen San Francisco.

last_week.label: No model
last_week.note: Same hour last week, with a bound sized the same way. The bar a model must beat.

chronos.label: Pretrained (Chronos-2)
chronos.note: Amazon's pretrained time-series model, used with no local fitting, with a bound sized the same way. E18's result, on this city.

fault_open.label: Broken, unwatched
fault_open.note: The reference model, but the plan is fed a third of its forecast: from the second week in the scored run, from noon on the first day in the recording.

fault_guarded.label: Broken, guarded
fault_guarded.note: The same broken feed, with a guard that hands control to a simple rule when the bound keeps breaking.
